title: Implementing a Promise/A+ subset from scratch
hook: LeetCode and Reddit senior threads ask you to implement Promise from scratch — not to ship it, but to prove you understand the state machine, then-chaining, and why callbacks run as microtasks. A minimal Promise/A+ subset is fifty lines; the bugs interviewers probe are double-resolution and missing return-value chaining.

blocks.text: A **Promise** is a state machine with three states: **pending**, **fulfilled**, and **rejected**. Once settled, it never changes again. The executor `(resolve, reject) => {}` runs synchronously when the Promise is constructed. **`.then(onFulfilled, onRejected)`** registers handlers and returns a new Promise that adopts the return value or rejection reason of the handler — this is **chaining**. Promise/A+ requires that `onFulfilled`/`onRejected` run asynchronously — in practice engines use the **microtask queue** (`queueMicrotask` or equivalent).

entries.plainDefinition: The (resolve, reject) => {} callback passed to new Promise — runs immediately, synchronously.
Any object with a .then method. Promises adopt thenable results.
Community spec that native Promise implements — chaining and assimilation rules.
entries.example: then must return a new Promise.

entries.plainDefinition: When a handler returns a thenable, the returned Promise waits for it to settle.
entries.example: return fetch(url) — outer Promise waits for fetch Promise.

blocks.text: Understanding the implementation explains real bugs: forgetting to return inside `.then` breaks chains, resolving twice is silently ignored in native Promise but breaks naive implementations, and throwing in a handler rejects the returned Promise. Libraries like axios and database drivers wrap callback APIs with `new Promise` — knowing the state machine helps you wrap Redis `get` or legacy `fs.readFile` correctly and test error paths.

blocks.title: Interview goal
blocks.body: Implement resolve, reject, then with microtask scheduling and return-value chaining. Full Promise.all is a common follow-up — not required in the first five minutes.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Call then while pending
items.body: Push onFulfilled/onRejected to a subscribers array.

items.title: Call then after fulfilled
items.body: Schedule onFulfilled(value) on microtask queue immediately.

items.title: Handler runs
items.body: If it returns a value, fulfill the child Promise. If it throws, reject child. If it returns a thenable, assimilate.

items.title: Return child Promise
items.body: Caller can chain .then on the returned Promise.

snippet.label: Minimal MyPromise — core state machine
snippet.explanation: Lines 8–10: ignore double resolve. Line 27: microtask async requirement. Lines 31–33: pass-through rejection without onRejected. Line 37: then returns new Promise for chaining.

snippet.label: Chaining and return-value adoption
snippet.explanation: Line 2: return value becomes next input. Line 3: throw rejects chain. Line 4: catch handler recovery returns string fulfilled to line 5.

snippet.label: Production — promisify Redis get
snippet.explanation: Lines 2–7: error-first callback → Promise wrapper is the daily pattern. Line 11: await uses native Promise microtasks even if getFromRedis uses custom wrapper.

snippet.label: Failure mode — sync resolve in executor
snippet.explanation: Line 4: executor throw after settle must not change state — native Promise ignores it. Line 12 in class: try/catch around executor handles throws before settle.

blocks.title: Calling handlers synchronously
blocks.body: Running onFulfilled immediately when resolve is called breaks ordering puzzles and fails Promise/A+. Always queueMicrotask.

blocks.title: Forgetting assimilation
blocks.body: If onFulfilled returns a thenable, the child Promise must wait — returning it directly fulfills with the thenable object, not its value.

blocks.text: Senior follow-ups: implement `catch` as `then(undefined, onRejected)`, add thenable assimilation with a `resolvePromise` helper, or implement `Promise.all`. In production, prefer native Promise — custom implementations appear in test mocks and embedded runtimes. The assimilation rule is what makes `return fetch(url)` inside then work. Interviewers reject answers that hand-wave 'it callbacks later' without naming microtasks.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Sync then callbacks. No return Promise from then. Cannot explain why resolve(2) then resolve(3) leaves value 2. Saying Promise.all is built into the constructor. Not connecting implementation to microtask ordering.

interviewTakeaways: Promise = pending | fulfilled | rejected; settle once.
then registers handlers; returns new Promise; schedules handlers on microtasks.
Return value or thrown error in handler drives the child Promise.

60s: State machine plus subscriber list. resolve/reject once. queueMicrotask for then. then returns new Promise. promisify wraps error-first callbacks. C# uses TaskCompletionSource for manual complete.
Follow-up: implement Promise.all or thenable assimilation.
commonPitfalls: Weak: synchronous then — breaks event-loop ordering.
Weak: no child Promise from then — chaining impossible.
Strong: 'Pending queues handlers. Settle fires microtasks. then returns new Promise adopting handler result or assimilation.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: TypeScript types resolve/reject values but implementation is identical at runtime. Return type of then is inferred from handler return.
Promise.all builds on the same then-chaining — interview often follows scratch Promise with all implementation.
